prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1313; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in on the roadway in Pasadena, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your current address for the file.

A: I'd rather just give the city and state for now. I live in Pasadena.

Q: That's fine. Can you walk me through what happened before the collision?

A: I was driving straight down the road, going maybe twenty-five miles an hour. The traffic was light. Then the other vehicle drifted into my lane.

Q: Did you have time to react?

A: Not really. I hit the brakes and turned a little to the right, but we still met nose to nose. It wasn't a hard impact, though. More of a jolt.

Q: Did either airbag deploy?

A: No, nothing deployed. The car just stopped pretty quickly.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?

A: I did. I stood by the car for a while, and then I sat down on the curb because my lower back felt tight.

Q: Have you sought medical attention since the collision?

A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic that afternoon. They said I had a back strain and gave me a muscle relaxer and told me to rest.

Q: Are you experiencing any symptoms now?

A: Yes, stiffness in the lower back, mostly in the morning. Sitting for long periods makes it worse. I've been limiting my driving.

Q: Did you have any prior injuries to your back?

A: Nothing serious. I had some soreness years ago from lifting boxes, but it went away and I hadn't had any trouble since.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Just that I'm trying to get back to normal and I'm following the treatment plan.

Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the recorded statement.
